historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.3% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 14.2% (>30% divergence). Revenue CAGR includes the Decmil civil acquisition (FY2024) and a mining-cycle upswing; equity CAGR is the better guide to organic compounding. Base-case year-1 growth is set at 5%, below the selected 6.3%, because FY26 is late-cycle and the FY28 segment targets imply mid-single-digit growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - lease principal): FY21 -28.8, FY22 -18.2, FY23 -12.7, FY24 36.8, FY25 73.5, FY26 86.9 (A$m). CAGRs from a negative base are undefined, so fcf_3yr/5yr are null; owner FCF was negative or near zero for FY21-23 while the fleet was being built. Reported FCF (28-40% CAGR) flatters the picture badly because IFRS-16 puts A$57-85m/yr of equipment lease principal in financing activities. Cumulative owner FCF FY22-26 is only ~A$167m against a ~A$2.36bn market cap, which is the core of the valuation gap.

scenario_narratives.base: Macmahon works through its A$5.9bn order book (about 2.25 years of revenue) at mid-single-digit growth: 5% in FY27-28 as civil and underground work ramps toward the FY28 targets, decelerating to 2.5% by FY33. EBITDA margin holds at 14.5-14.7%, the low end of its seven-year 14.7-18.3% band, because civil infrastructure carries lower margins than surface mining. The FY26 capital-intensity trough (capex + lease principal 8.0% of revenue) is normalised to 9.5%, still well below the 12% seven-year average, giving management credit for the stated strategy of reducing capital intensity. Cash tax at the 30% statutory rate; single 10% AUD WACC; terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF, a cyclical-contractor multiple. The result is an owner-FCF margin of roughly 3.5% of revenue, which is what the business has actually delivered in its best years.
scenario_narratives.bull: The civil business reaches $1bn and underground $750m+ ahead of the FY28 target, Indonesia scales to 20% of group revenue, and the Batu Hijau relationship (AMNT is both the largest customer and a 44% shareholder) keeps extending. Growth runs 8% for two years, EBITDA margin recovers to the underlying 15.5%, and the lower-capital-intensity mix holds capex + lease principal at 8.5-9.0% of revenue permanently. The terminal cap is lifted to 14x owner FCF to reflect a business the market would treat as a diversified services company rather than a fleet-heavy mining contractor. This is the re-rating thesis the current price is paying for.
scenario_narratives.bear: A commodity-price downturn or the loss/downsizing of a major surface contract (two customers are 29% of revenue) removes ~8% of revenue over FY28-29. Fixed fleet costs and idle equipment compress EBITDA margin to 12.5% and hold D&A at ~9% while capex is cut; margin only partially recovers to 13.5%. Revenue growth resumes at 2-2.5%. The terminal cap falls to 10x, the multiple this stock carried through most of the last decade. The balance sheet survives (net debt ex-leases is near zero, A$550m facility to 2030), so this is an earnings and multiple bear, not a solvency bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Macmahon is a fleet-heavy contract miner diversifying into civil and underground work. Reported FCF flatters it by A$60-85m a year because IFRS-16 puts equipment lease principal in financing; on an owner basis the business converted only ~A$167m of cumulative cash to shareholders over FY22-26. The valuation therefore rests on normalised capital intensity, not on the FY26 trough, and on a terminal multiple appropriate to a cyclical contractor (10-14x owner FCF). A 10% AUD WACC is applied once; cycle risk is carried in the bear scenario and its 25% weight.
key_risks_to_valuation: Customer concentration: two customers = A$760m (29%) of FY26 revenue; AMNT (Batu Hijau) is also a 44.27% shareholder, which cuts both ways -- contract security versus governance.
Capital intensity: FY26 capex + lease principal of 8.0% of revenue is a cyclical low; every 1pp of normalised capex is ~A$26-37m/yr of owner FCF, roughly 30% of the base-case FCF stream.
Commodity cycle: surface mining revenue follows gold, copper and lithium (Greenbushes) volumes; the FY21 fleet build shows how fast capital demand rises in an upswing.
Margin: civil infrastructure is lower-margin and carries fixed-price project risk (Decmil legacy); the base assumes margin holds at the seven-year floor.
Cash tax: FY24-25 benefited from carried-forward losses now exhausted; 30% statutory is the run-rate.
Guidance vintage: no numeric FY27 guidance in the extracted filings; the August-2026 results presentation range is the first thing to check on refresh.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 0.395-1.145 AUD
data_sources.financials: MAH.AX_Metrics.csv / MAH.AX.duckdb core_metrics and kpis (FY2016-FY2026 annual + half-years), anchored to MAH.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt: cash flow statement (lines 7778-7804), note 18 borrowings roll-forward (9655-9700: interest-bearing loans 325,961k / lease liabilities 94,777k), note 4 lease interest 6,342k (8240), diluted shares (8523), major customers (7999)
data_sources.qualitative: MAH.AX_Analysis.json not yet written at build time; narrative drawn from the FY2026 annual report (Chair/CEO letters, financial review, outlook) and the H1-FY2026 results presentation (FY26 guidance and FY28 targets, line 630)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average for FY2026 (MAH.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:8523, 2,175,731,992); basic WA 2,141.1m; shares on issue ~2,155m. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). No non-SBC issuance planned; last equity raise was for the Decmil acquisition (FY2024).
inputs.sbc_source: MAH.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:7569 share-based payments expense $4,993k (cash flow add-back; no net-share-settlement tax withholding disclosed, so no equity-award tax component)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-23T06:10:05Z (ASX regular close; not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built rate: AU 10-year government bond ~4.3% (Sep-2026) + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.2 = ~10.9% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~6.5% (syndicated facility, BBSW + margin) x (1-30%) = 4.55%; market-weight gearing ~12% (A$326m loans vs ~A$2.36bn market cap) -> WACC 10.1%, rounded to 10.0%. Single WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality and customer concentration are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating/capital cost, NOT debt). Macmahon finances mining fleet through finance leases and a syndicated asset-finance facility: FY26 lease principal repaid A$63.1m (financing activities), lease interest A$6.3m (note 4). Lease principal is charged as capex-equivalent in capex_pct_path (capex 145.8 + lease principal 63.1 = 208.9m = 8.0% of FY26 revenue); lease interest is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (0.24% of revenue); D&A (which includes depreciation of leased plant) is the tax deduction for those assets, so there is no double charge. Lease liabilities (A$94.8m) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt: net_debt = interest-bearing loans 325.961 - cash 309.653 = 16.308 (company-reported net debt of 111.1m includes the 94.8m of leases).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are 100% attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (cyclical / non-US adaptations applied) -- Macmahon is a contract mining and civil-infrastructure services company (surface mining, underground mining, civil, Indonesia), an operating company whose value is its owner cash flow stream. OWNER FCF FY2026: reported FCF (OCF 300.758 - capex 145.79 = 154.968) - SBC 4.993 - lease principal 63.055 = 86.92; lease interest is already inside OCF (net interest paid 30.6m) so it is not deducted again here. Interest income (2.49m on 310m cash) is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt on the ex-lease basis (loans 326m vs cash 310m), and the cash is netted against the drawn syndicated facility in the bridge, so there is no double-count. MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: EBITDA margin has been stable at 14.7-18.3% for seven years, so the cycle shows up in capital intensity, not margin -- capex + lease principal ran 8.0% (FY26 trough, 'lower capital expenditure incurred on new work' and two Surface projects completed) to 19.8% (FY21 fleet build) of revenue, 7-year average ~12%. The structural shift to civil and underground (lower capital intensity, management's stated strategy) argues for a lower normal than the 7-year average, so base capex is normalised to 9.0% FY27 rising to 9.5% and tapering to 9.2% terminal, against D&A of 8.0-8.5%. FY26 cash tax (53.2m, 36% of pre-tax) was a catch-up after carried-forward losses were exhausted in FY24-25; 30% statutory is used throughout. Working capital: contractor with receivables + contract assets > payables, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture -3% of incremental revenue; FY24-26 OCF reconciliation shows WC swings of -16 / +28 / -1m, near zero on average). Buybacks: none in FY26 (2.8m FY25 was for employee-share-plan purchases); the flat count is a modelling convention funded by SBC expensing, not by repurchases. GUIDANCE: FY26 guidance ($2.6-2.8bn revenue, $180-195m underlying EBIT(A)) was met at $2.62bn / $190.1m. No numeric FY27 guidance appears in the extracted filings (the FY26 annual says only 'positive outlook for FY27'; the August-2026 results presentation carrying the FY27 range is not in the folder) -- year-1 growth is therefore anchored on the A$5.9bn order book (2.25 years of revenue) and the FY28 segment targets (underground >$750m, civil $1bn, Indonesia 15-20%), and the FY27 guidance range is the evidence that would move it. Statutory EBITDA (operating profit + D&A) is used as the margin anchor (14.7%); underlying EBITDA was 393.8m (15.0%).

bear.narrative: Commodity downturn or a large surface contract roll-off: revenue falls ~8% over FY28-29, margin compresses to 12.5% on fixed fleet costs, D&A stays high on an under-utilised fleet, terminal multiple at the historical trough.

base.narrative: Order book converts at mid-single-digit growth; margin holds at the 7-year floor as civil mix rises; capex normalises from the FY26 trough to ~9.5% then tapers as the fleet build slows.

bull.narrative: FY28 targets hit early (civil $1bn, underground $750m+), Indonesia scales to 20%, capital intensity structurally lower, margin recovers toward the underlying 15.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: mining services is cyclical, two customers are 29% of revenue, and the stock has re-rated 175% in twelve months on a business whose cumulative five-year owner FCF is ~7% of its market cap. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs the FY28 segment targets, a benign commodity cycle, a permanent capital-intensity step-down and a multiple re-rating to all hold at once. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
